newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cardoso calls social critics "neofools".
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cardoso calls social critics "neofools".

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso defended his government's record on improving social conditions in Brazil and dismissed critics as "neofools," newspapers reported.

"Only those who have nothing inside their heads keep repeating that the government is only worried about the market, that it is neoliberal. That is neofoolism," the newspapers quoted the president as saying.

The president was speaking at the swearing in Monday of new directors of the Community Solidarity Program, a body set up by Cardoso to coordinate the government's poverty relief efforts and which is presided over by his wife, Ruth Cardoso.

The president, whose government is widely perceived as doing little on issues such as health and education, recalled how his government had doubled to seven million the number of food baskets distributed free to Brazil's poor.
He also criticized left-wing opposition parties for failing to include special credits, which are added to budget allocations, when accusing the government of cutting spending on social services.
